entries.english:
Photographs on Jewish life and National Socialism in Ahlen 2

Views of Ahlen, postcards, and family photographs of Jewish families (originals and reproductions) from H.W. Gummersbach’s book, including: 1: Imo Moszkowicz’s first visit to Ahlen secondary school, 1985; 2: former Gumpert house, Oststraße, c. 1985; 3–5: Rottmannstraße 28, former factory, formerly rented by Rosa Rosenberg; 6–7: various houses in the town centre (Oststraße, Warendorfer Straße), 1985; 8: former Levi Rosenberg house, Kampstraße, 1985; 9: former Auerbach house, later Radio Sib, Nordstraße, 1985; 10: former Dreyer property / Hanni Katzenstein, Bismarckstraße 33; 11: Oststraße, 1990; 12: flat at Im Kühl 21 occupied by various Jewish residents (Mannheimer, Rothschild, Schöne), 1990; 13: “Eduscho,” Oststraße, 1990; 14: former A. S. Rosenberg factory, Beckumer Straße (photograph and accompanying letter from Heinz Hartmann to Gummersbach), 1992; 15: reproduction of Ahlen public baths; 16: Westenmauer, 1990; 17–24: various views (Oststraße; Bismarckstraße, illustration in book p. 59; Nordstraße; Südenmauer; Herz Spiegel house; illustrations in book pp. 77–79); 25: Gerichtsstraße, c. 1990; 26: Hansastraße: Woolworth, Helm bakery, c. 1985; 27: Hansa-Eck, former Frieda David shop, Hansastraße (book p. 208); 28: Jewish cemetery, c. 1990; 29: second exhibition marking 30 January 1933 in the Lohnhalle; H.W. Gummersbach guides residents of the Ahlen colony, 1984; 30: dedication of the memorial on Klosterstraße, November 1985; 31: Heiner Lichtenfels and Frieda Spiegel on their visit to Ahlen, November 1985; 32–36: discussions between Ahlen school pupils and Holocaust survivors, including Mr. Wolffs, 1985; 37: exhibition “The road to Auschwitz also began in Ahlen,” 1990; 38: visit to Münster in 1985 with Frieda Spiegel, Hans Sänger (Jerusalem), and Lichtenfels; 39: H.W. Gummersbach with Irma Wolffs in Ahlen, 1985; 40: Irma Wolffs in Switzerland, 1984; 41: Lilly and Walter Loewy, Haifa, 1986; 42: Gitte and H.W. Gummersbach with Frieda Spiegel, November 1985; also negatives of some prints. Also contains photocopies of historical newspaper clippings (1898, 1968–1984, including on demolition of buildings in the town centre); photocopies, including from Marga Spiegel’s life story and obituaries.

A collection of town-centre photographs from the Nazi period (c. 1937) was removed and catalogued separately under S 5 Ahlen.
